purpose: Draft-only human reasoning assessment criteria; not an automated scorer, canonical contract or mastery updater
criteria_policy: All required criteria must be evidenced; alternative mathematically valid justifications accepted by reviewer

criteria.description: States that the same whole is partitioned into three equal parts
Identifies 3 as denominator determining the number of equal parts of one whole
Identifies 2 as numerator counting two of those equal parts

acceptable_evidence: Three equal parts in a whole; numerator two means two parts are considered
Denominator 3 means thirds; numerator 2 means two thirds
non_evidence: 2 out of 3 without explaining numerator and denominator
common_errors: Treats denominator as the number shaded
rubrics.decision: Human reviewer confirms all three criteria. Numeric answer alone never establishes conceptual mastery.

criteria.description: Shows both equal 1/2, or a correct same-value area/number-line argument, or correct cross-products 2×6=4×3=12

rubrics.decision: Correct yes/no alone is insufficient; a reviewer must verify mathematically valid justification.

rubrics.prompt_focus: Choose 6/8 or 6/12 as equivalent to 3/4 and explain

criteria.description: Demonstrates 6/8=3/4 by factor 2 or simplification, and distinguishes 6/12=1/2

rubrics.decision: Both selection and contrast must be mathematically valid; no automatic reasoning credit.

criteria.description: Simplifies both to 2/3 or demonstrates correct cross-product equality 4×15=6×10=60

rubrics.decision: Human reviewer verifies both verdict and justification.
